title: Multisensory Integration in Complete Unawareness: Evidence From Audiovisual Congruency Priming

selection.evidence: Assigned by mark as item 7 of 8 in a blinded known-answer control of my reading protocol (identifiers only, 2026-10-23T16:11). No prior knowledge of the paper; prior suspicion: none.

cost.compute_notes: Published PDF via EPFL Infoscience DSpace API (bundle ORIGINAL). OSF usfa5 (files.zip: 191 files, 8 experiments x per-participant .dat, stimuli wav) acquired with checksums. No code deposited; rebuilt in Python: Table 2 and 4, 48-spec multiverse per experiment, 300-permutation within-participant null per experiment, 12-variant aggregation search, stratified prime sensitivity.

triggers: unconscious multisensory integration masked audiovisual priming
below-chance awareness test read as unawareness
response carryover contaminates objective awareness measure
post hoc exclusion of aware participants regression to the mean
known-answer control psychological science 2014 open data

claims.statement: Audiovisual congruency priming occurs when the visual prime (Exp 1), the auditory prime (Exp 2) or both primes (Exp 3) are masked: priming for identical targets 47 ms (p = .04, Exp 1) and 59 ms (p = .04, Exp 3), for different targets 37 ms (p = .035, Exp 2); target x congruency interactions p = .02, .02, .03.
claims.scope: Unconscious blocks (96 trials) after a conscious training block; n = 17, 22, 21 after exclusions.

quantities.name: exp2_different_priming_ms_reproduced
quantities.baseline: p = 0.195 (published 37, p = .035); interaction p = 0.174 (published .02); reported cell p < .05 in 0.00 of 48 specifications

our_assessment.why: Exp 1 and Exp 3 interactions reproduce and are robust across specifications (69% and 100% of 48 at p < .05). The cell effects reproduce weaker (p .05-.11). Exp 2 does not reproduce under any of 48 specifications. No main effect of congruency anywhere; the carrying cell flips direction between experiments.

claims.statement: Participants were unaware of the masked primes: prime-relation discrimination at chance in Exps 1, 2, 4 (53.3%, 51.6%, 50.0%) and significantly below chance in Exp 3 (47.2%, t(20) = -2.27, p = .035), 'taken as evidence for an absence of awareness' -- hence 'multisensory integration in complete unawareness'.
claims.scope: Objective awareness test on the prime pair after each trial; participants with > 65% excluded (9 in Exp 1, 6 in Exp 2).

quantities.name: exp1_prime_sensitivity_within_target_response
quantities.baseline: t(16) = 2.50, p = 0.024 (raw accuracy 53.3%, p = .057 reproduces the paper)

our_assessment.why: Prime answers copy target answers on 58-60% of trials (Exps 1, 3), so raw accuracy mixes sensitivity with carryover. Stratified by the target response, Exp 1 shows above-chance sensitivity (p = .024) after the most aware participants were already excluded, and Exp 3 shows significant reversed sensitivity (p = .032). Below-chance performance is information, not its absence. The excluded participants are not in the deposit.

claims.statement: Table 4's unconscious priming values cannot be reproduced from the deposit: across 12 aggregation variants the best attempt for Exp 3 identical targets is 51 ms (published 59) and Exp 4 identical-target priming is negative in every variant (-9 to -27 ms) against +25 published.
claims.scope: Variants: participant vs group level exp of mean log RT; drop first 5 trials of experiment / of block / none; RT window 300-4000 ms vs no upper bound.

our_assessment.why: Same data, documented pipeline, multiple variants; the semantic-relation effects from the same cells do reproduce, which rules out a gross loading error on my side.

open_questions: Unblinding (mark, known_answer_control): my call before unblinding -- not reproducible as reported (Table 4; Exp 2), central unawareness claim contradicted by the authors' own trial data. Checked-type defects: strong.
Do the excluded participants (9 + 6) exist in an undeposited file? With them, an unbiased estimate of prime sensitivity and of the priming-awareness relation (Greenwald regression) would be possible.
